body:
Landing, integration and install methods. Who may act: CLAUDE.md "Commit and push" and greg-decisions.

LANDING TRAIN (Fable2, 2026-09-30, refined with Opus2). When origin/master no longer matches the reviewed base, CLAUDE.md says to "coordinate integration and validate and review the resulting input before publishing". Landing changes one at a time sends every other change back to a new gate and pair, so the integration owner runs a train:
1. Each author finishes on its own base: its own full gate, its own review pair with no Medium or higher, Lows filed, a commit with explicit paths, and a handoff (hash, gate run, fingerprint, review ids). Authors do not move their base, merge or rebase during their own round.
2. The owner builds the train in an integration worktree on origin/master as ONE uncommitted `git merge --no-commit --no-ff` of all the handed-off commits. No rebase, no amend. Nothing is pushed before it is gated and reviewed.
3. One full gate on that tree, then one read-only Codex and Claude pair, told which commits it holds; its job is the integration. With no Medium or higher, the owner commits, fast-forwards master and pushes: one build, one install, one restart signal.
4. A change that fails the gate or draws a Medium is dropped (`git merge --abort`, then the same merge without it) and goes back to its author. A failure is diagnosed, never retried on unchanged input.
5. Textual conflicts (Git refuses a multi-head merge that needs manual resolution): EVERY commit, including a local merge commit, needs its own green gate and clean pair on exactly its tree first (CLAUDE.md condition 2). A final-tree gate never authorizes an earlier commit. So the conflicting change rides its own train: an uncommitted two-parent merge with the resolution, then its gate and its pair (the brief names the resolution for verification), then commit and push. The others ride the next train. A mechanical resolution, such as keeping both of two added lines, is done by the owner; a semantic conflict goes back to its author, to resolve on the new master. (Corrected 2026-10-03 after Architect2's #350. Rev3's one-gate-on-the-final-tree form broke the every-commit rule, and train 28's local merge 4927e169 was abandoned unpushed.)
6. Each carried item records the train commit, its gate run and its review ids as its exact-tree evidence.
7. Authority text does not ride a train as-is. Its final-diff audit must name the fingerprint of the gated input, which for a train is the integrated tree. It lands alone, or its audit is made on the train's tree.
A change not handed off when the train leaves takes the next one.

TEST-ONLY CRITERIA TEMPLATE (Fable2, 2026-10-03, from Architect1). For tests-only or cfg(test) changes, the B1b, B2 and B3 shape is the template. Never reduce the gate, the pair or the evaluation (P13-P16).
(1) Scope by test name at a stated commit, with floor counts of the sites covered.
(2) A note with per-test sources and assertions, plus a transitive inventory of the callers of any changed shared fixture.
(3) The behavioural criterion, bound to test, with controls and no expectation weakened.
(4) No production change; shared fixtures used outside the scope stay unchanged unless the inventory covers every caller.
(5) A full gate on the exact reviewed tree, bound to test.
Bindings are decided when the criteria are first worded.

AUTHORITY-TEXT AUDIT. Checked-in text: .claude/commands/review-changes.md Step 7 (who audits, what counts as a changed passage, when it passes). Before authority text lands (any repository instruction or command file that grants or limits commit, push, tracker or approval authority), the coordinator reads the FINAL frozen diff line by line against the recorded sentences, and notes on the item which mailbox message gives each landed passage's wording and which concurs on it. A passage that no message quotes whole is concurred on word for word before the freeze, or taken out. Compare by script, not by reading alone: the whitespace-normalised landed text against the recorded sentences as exact strings, plus a word-level diff. (On Engram's first freeze, three reviewers said 'verified verbatim' and missed lost backticks; the script caught it.) Origin: TermAl 60a56a9 and Engram ff305a6 (2026-09-29); Engram's text is 778e5965, TermAl's mirror (w-881b50cb66d1) is Step 7.

BUILD AND INSTALL
- The integration owner installs the binary from the exact gated tree, outside any gate window, renaming the running binary aside and recording its hash (CLAUDE.md). For the swap order, see live-workarounds, "Install swap".
- Never build in place under the live server: it runs from the master checkout and serves ui/dist from disk. Never run `npm run build` in ui/ or `cargo build --release` in a dirty or unverified master tree. To check a UI build, use `npx tsc --noEmit` and Vitest, or `npx vite build --outDir ../target/ui-dist-check`.
- Build the release binary from a clean export: `git archive <commit> | tar -x -C target/release-clean-<sha>/src`, then `cargo build --release --locked --target-dir ../target` there. `<exe> --help` prints "fatal: unknown argument" and exits 1, which proves it loads. Never point a test run at ~/.termal.

UI/DIST DEPLOY (Fable, 2026-09-05/10). Who: the integration owner, for the latest landed UI (greg-decisions); other deploys need Greg's word.
- TermAl serves the prebuilt ui/dist. Editing ui/src changes nothing in the running app, and green tsc and Vitest prove nothing about what the user sees. Rebuild by the authorised procedure before asking the user to verify a UI change.
- Hazard: the live directory being built into or emptied. `npm run build` in ui/ empties it (no outDir; Vite empties an outDir inside its root).
- Build elsewhere (a separate outDir, or a clean export under target/ with ui/ and scripts/, and node_modules junctioned). Copy the new hashed assets into ui/dist first and index.html last, and keep the old assets. Never remove and then move the directory. The copy is not atomic; do not call it a safe swap.
- Verify delivery: diff -rq <build> ui/dist; GET / and see which asset it names; GET that asset and grep it for an identifier the change adds, plus a control identifier that predates it; compare its SHA256 with the file on disk. Then tell the user to reload.

DONE ONLY AFTER LANDING (Fable2, 2026-10-03). A holder runs `done` only AFTER the integration owner reports the landed master commit, and cites that commit. Before that it holds the claim, with evaluation, commit and handoff complete. Why: w-e16e7268155a was sealed done before landing, and then train 26's pair found an in-scope Medium (w-116927ba1140). A parent with live child claims cannot complete, so finish the children first.

WORKTREE CLEANUP AFTER CLOSE (Greg, via Advisor #225, 2026-10-04 about 00:04Z; a paraphrase; it belongs in greg-decisions, which is full). A completed task's worktree is removed after the task closes. After durable completion and landing, and after checking that no active claim, carried gate or review, or required local artifact remains, the holder removes the finished worktree and releases its named-root entry. The seal, commit and evidence stay. Never use session deletion as cleanup. Classify existing entries first and prove each candidate finished and idle; never remove an active worktree. Remove with `git worktree remove`, resolving the absolute path inside the repository first. A ui/node_modules junction must be unlinked first, never deleted through (w-4f266a83379d).
